passage: I'm Shankar, and last term I was admin of our class chat. It gave me a little tap-and-they're-gone power over everyone, and I liked that. One night Lokesh sent a long, boring voice note about cricket stats, and three loud boys wrote, "Remove him lol." My finger was already on his name. It would have been easy, and they'd have cheered for me. But I saw that they wanted a show, and that Lokesh would see the notification alone in his room. It made my stomach tight. I didn't remove him. I posted, "Voice notes under a minute please, everyone," and made the rule for everyone. The loud boys grumbled for a day. Lokesh sent me a thumbs up. I've thought since about how nice it felt to hold that button, and how quickly I could have used it to hurt someone.

qa.q: What kind of message did Lokesh send that night?
qa.a: He sent a long voice note about cricket stats.

qa.q: What was Shankar thinking with a finger already on Lokesh's name?
qa.a: Shankar knew it would be easy and the loud boys would cheer, but saw that they wanted a show and that Lokesh would see it alone. The tight stomach shows unease.

qa.q: What could Shankar do in future to use admin power fairly?
qa.a: Shankar can keep making rules that apply to everybody, like the one-minute voice note limit, and never remove anyone just to please the loud ones.

qa.q: How might Lokesh have felt if Shankar had removed him?
qa.a: Humiliated and alone. Getting a thumbs-up instead suggests he felt relieved and respected.

grounding: Shankar enjoys the control of being group admin but uses it fairly instead of removing someone to please the loud ones.

passage:
Sharmila was admin of the girls' cricket team group in Bhadrawati village, and she liked it more than she admitted. One tap, and someone was in. One tap, and they were out.
On Sunday, after Rukmini dropped an easy catch, three of the loudest girls started messaging: "Remove her. She's useless. Do it, Sharmila."
Sharmila's thumb hovered over the button. It would be easy. The loud girls would cheer. For a second she enjoyed the idea of everyone waiting on her decision.
Then she pictured Rukmini at practice, walking five kilometres from the next village every Saturday, always first on the field.
Sharmila typed instead: "Nobody's getting removed for one dropped catch. We've all dropped them. Rukmini, extra fielding practice with me on Tuesday?"
The loud girls went quiet. Rukmini replied with a thumbs-up and, a minute later, "Thank you."

qa.q: How far does Rukmini walk to practice every Saturday?
qa.a: Five kilometres from the next village.

qa.q: What was Sharmila feeling as her thumb hovered over the button?
qa.a: She felt a brief thrill of power, enjoying that everyone was waiting on her decision.

qa.q: What did Sharmila do with her admin power, and why was it fair?
qa.a: She refused to remove Rukmini for one dropped catch and offered extra practice, instead of pleasing the loud girls.

qa.q: How might Rukmini feel reading Sharmila's message?
qa.a: Rukmini likely feels relieved and grateful, protected from being humiliated and kicked out.

grounding: A teen admin enjoys the power to remove people but uses it fairly, refusing to exclude a teammate to please the loud ones.

passage:
Tuan had set up the robotics club chat for their Melbourne school at the start of the year, which made him admin. He hadn't expected to like it so much. He could pin messages, mute people, remove them with one tap.
On Thursday, Rafael, the loudest boy in the club, messaged him privately: "Kick Oliver. His code crashed our robot at the demo. Everyone's annoyed."
Tuan looked at the member list. Oliver was quiet, new, and the only Year 8. Removing him would make Rafael happy. It would also humiliate Oliver in front of everyone.
Tuan felt the pull of it: the power to decide, the approval of the loud ones.
He wrote back: "Not removing anyone for a bug. That's what debugging is for." Then, in the main chat: "Team session on Friday to fix the code together. Oliver, want to walk us through it?"
Rafael sent an eye-roll. Oliver sent: "Yes!"

qa.q: Why did Rafael want Oliver removed?
qa.a: Oliver's code crashed their robot at the demo.

qa.q: What was Tuan feeling when Rafael asked him to kick Oliver?
qa.a: He felt the pull of power and the wish for the loud boys' approval, while also sensing it would humiliate Oliver.

qa.q: Which choice did Tuan make as admin, and why was it wise?
qa.a: He refused to remove Oliver for a bug and invited him to lead a fixing session, using his power fairly instead of to humiliate.

qa.q: How might Rafael see Tuan's decision?
qa.a: Rafael seems annoyed, sending an eye-roll, because he wanted Oliver gone and didn't get his way.

grounding: A teen group admin enjoys the power to remove people but uses it fairly instead of excluding someone to please the loud ones.
